description.label: Description
description.value:
You call out to the Ancient Widow, reminding her of her promises to Khan-Queen Shoika, first Tzarina of Kislev, and cause 20-foot tendrils of ice to erupt from the ground. All creatures in the area has their Movement halved and must succeed a Challenging (+0) Athletics Test each round or the tendrils wrap around them dealing SB+4 Damage that ignores armor and count as having the @Compendium[wfrp4e-core.items.KynNUYYKzTMeHrKl]{Constrictor} Creature Trait. The tendrils count as having a Weapon Skill equal to yours and Strength equal to your Intelligence Characteristic.

 

Lore : The flows of Ice Magic vary in strength. By Kislev’s sites of power, along her leylines, in freezing climates and in the depths of winter, Ice Magic is very strong, granting you a +10 to all @Compendium[wfrp4e-core.items.V8eRx66SxB9Jha0Q]{Channelling} and @Compendium[wfrp4e-core.items.e3McIND4Rrsn5cE6]{Language (Magick)} Tests when casting the Lore of Ice. But in warmer climes, it is far weaker and wanes the closer to the equator and the further from the North one travels. When casting in warmer climates, such as in most of the Empire, it counts as if casting next to a Corrupting Influence, causing a @Table[minormis] on a unit’s roll of an 8. If you already have a @Table[minormis], the Miscast becomes a @Table[majormis]. In hotter climates, such as in a desert or jungle, you receive a permanent @Condition[Fatigued] Condition until you relocate to a cooler climate. You may spend a Resolve point to mitigate this Fatigue Condition for one round.
